stories.headline: Bahrain Proposes UN Resolution Authorizing 'All Necessary Means' to Protect Hormuz Shipping

key_facts.fact: Bahrain circulated a draft UN Security Council resolution authorizing countries to use 'all necessary means' including within territorial waters of littoral states to secure transit passage in the Strait of Hormuz
key_facts.excerpt: The text would authorize countries, acting alone or through voluntary multinational naval coalitions, to use 'all necessary means' in and around the Strait of Hormuz – including in the territorial waters of littoral states – to ensure passage

key_facts.fact: The draft resolution calls Iran's actions a threat to international peace and security and demands Iran immediately cease all attacks against merchant vessels
key_facts.excerpt: The draft, seen by The National, accuses Iran of repeated attacks and threats against merchant shipping, and says its actions are a threat to international peace and security

key_facts.fact: The draft is backed by other Gulf Arab states and the US, but diplomats say it is unlikely to succeed
key_facts.excerpt: Diplomats said the draft text was backed by other Gulf Arab states and the United States, although they said it was unlikely to succeed

key_facts.fact: Only a trickle of cargo ships and tankers, mostly Iranian, have made it through the Strait since Iran effectively blocked it three weeks ago; normally about 1/5 of global crude oil and LNG passes through
key_facts.excerpt: Just a trickle of cargo ships and tankers, most of them Iranian, have made it through the Strait since Iran effectively blocked it... Normally, about a fifth of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas pass through the Strait

key_facts.fact: The resolution also expresses readiness to impose targeted sanctions on Iran
key_facts.excerpt: The resolution also expresses the readiness to impose measures, including targeted sanctions

stories.headline: Celosia Therapeutics Doses First ALS Patient in Gene Therapy Targeting TDP-43 Protein

key_facts.excerpt: today announced dosing of the first participant in its Phase 1b KOANEWA trial evaluating CTx1000, an investigational genetic medicine targeting pathological forms of the TDP-43 protein in people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis

key_facts.fact: CTx1000 is designed to selectively bind and clear toxic forms of TDP-43; in preclinical models it halted disease progression and in some cases partially reversed disease manifestations

key_facts.fact: The trial is conducted at Macquarie University Hospital in Sydney, Australia, registered as NCT07401121
key_facts.excerpt: The study is being conducted at the Neurology Department of Macquarie University Hospital in Sydney, Australia
